issues.legal_issue: A premium-cut decision made before a later restriction on cancelling quasi-permanent allotments took effect is not invalidated by that later restriction.
material_facts: The authorities approved a 50% premium cut for land in villages considered semi-urban before the relevant restriction was added to the rules.
The land allotted to the appellant was close to a municipal area and its semi-urban character had not been taken into account when the original allotment was made.
The later rule contained no indication that it applied retrospectively.
issues.conclusion: The action taken before the later restriction was promulgated was valid and in accordance with law, and the scheme had been altered before that restriction took effect.
issues.legal_principle: A later rule does not invalidate earlier action where the rule contains no express or implied direction that it operates retrospectively. Rule 14(6) of the Evacuee Property (Central) Rules, 1950 was amended after the decision at issue. Basant Ram v. Union of India concerned the effect of the 1954 Act and the transfer of evacuee property to the compensation pool; Hukum Chand v. Union of India concerned retrospective rule-making without statutory authority; Hoshnak Singh v. Union of India was distinguished on its different facts.

predicates.appeal_challenging_reduced_allotment: An allottee appealed against a decision enforcing a reduced land allotment.
predicates.adjustment_order_preceded_later_restrict: The authorities made the adjustment decision before a later restriction on cancellation took effect.
predicates.later_restriction_contained_no_retroacti: The later restriction did not state that it applied to decisions already made.

issues.definition: When an allottee challenges a reduced allotment, an adjustment made before a later restriction that does not apply retrospectively remains valid.

issues.legal_issue: A displaced allottee is not entitled to retain an unadjusted allotment of semi-urban land when the same adjustment was applied to similarly situated allottees.
material_facts: The original allotment did not account for the land's semi-urban character.
Of 117 allottees in the affected villages, 97 paid the extra premium and were allowed to acquire their entire allotments.
The appellant was among the allottees who challenged the premium and reduction, although the allottees stood equally with respect to the adjustment decision.
issues.conclusion: There was no justification for granting the appellant the benefit claimed or treating the appellant differently from the other allottees. The authorities were not precluded from considering an offer to pay the extra premium or any further amount to obtain a lawful settlement of the entire property.
issues.legal_principle: Under the compensation scheme for displaced persons, settlement of evacuee land was intended to compensate for land left behind, not to permit undue enrichment. Where the land's semi-urban character was omitted from the original allotment, a corresponding adjustment could be just and fair, and similarly situated allottees should not receive differential treatment without justification. The Court considered Basant Ram v. Union of India, Hukum Chand v. Union of India and Hoshnak Singh v. Union of India, distinguishing the last on its facts; it did not treat those cases as requiring the benefit claimed here.

predicates.appeal_challenging_reduced_allotment: An allottee appealed against a decision reducing an earlier land allotment.
predicates.original_allotment_omitted_semi_urban_ch: The original allotment did not account for the land's semi-urban character.
predicates.similarly_situated_allottees_received_sa: Other allottees in the same position were subject to the same adjustment.

issues.definition: An allottee whose original allotment omitted the land's semi-urban character is not entitled to retain it without adjustment when similarly situated allottees received the same adjustment.
